content:
Earlier this month, OpenAI, together with Astra, launched its first GPT-6 model. The GPT-6 series officially debuts, adding two variants—GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna—further expanding the product lineup.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are available starting today

According to the ChatGPT desktop app's update notes, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna consume fewer tokens than their corresponding GPT-5.6 versions.

GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna will be available on Codex and ChatGPT Work, with token pricing lower than the previous-generation GPT-5.6. Sol is suited for complex coding and intelligent agent workflows, while Luna is designed for tasks requiring high focus and high throughput. Both models will be rolled out in phases to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users. Free and Go users can access Luna via the desktop app. Actual availability will depend on the rollout schedule and workspace settings; Enterprise administrators will need to enable the new models themselves. Within ChatGPT, both models are currently only available on Work and Codex, and have not yet arrived on Chat.

Worth noting: there is no so-called GPT-6 Terra. It appears OpenAI is phasing out mid-tier models, retaining only three tiers: Terra (small), Sol (large), Astra (extra-large).

Below is OpenAI's official announcement:

Even though the most challenging and high-impact tasks still require Astra's full depth, different tasks have different scales, rhythms, and budgets. For this reason, we are expanding the GPT-6 series with the launch of GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra pioneered a new generation of intelligence, and these two new models further enhance cost-effectiveness, bringing these advantages to a broader range of users. We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna using the same methods used to train GPT-6 Astra, distilling Astra's leading capabilities in professional work, factual accuracy, coding, computer use, and model alignment into faster, more economical models.

The company stated that both new models outperform GPT-5.6, with pricing also lower than Astra (as well as the GPT-5.6 versions they replace). For example, the Sol and Luna versions of GPT-6 are priced 50% lower than their GPT-5.6 counterparts.
